name: Primary Pericardial Mesothelioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Pericardial Mesothelioma

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of malignant mesothelial cells in pericardial tissue
Positive immunohistochemical staining for mesothelial markers (e.g., calretinin, WT-1, cytokeratin 5/6)
Imaging evidence of pericardial thickening or mass on echocardiography, CT, or MRI
Exclusion of metastatic carcinoma or other primary tumors involving the pericardium

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus positive immunohistochemical staining; imaging and exclusion criteria support diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Definitive diagnosis requires tissue biopsy with immunohistochemical confirmation due to overlap with other pericardial malignancies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive pericardial effusion with tamponade physiology
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic accumulation of fluid causing cardiac compression
searchTerms: increasing fluid around heart causing pressure
progressive pericardial fluid with tamponade signs

pathognomonic.symptomName: Constriction of the pericardium leading to restrictive cardiac physiology
pathognomonic.notes: Fibrotic thickening causing impaired diastolic filling
searchTerms: stiff heart covering limiting heart function

common.symptomName: Dyspnea on exertion due to impaired cardiac function
Chest pain of pleuritic or constrictive nature
searchTerms: chest pain worsened by breathing or heart constriction

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to decreased cardiac output
common.notes: Generalized weakness and reduced exercise tolerance
searchTerms: fatigue due to low cardiac output

common.notes: Occasional atrial fibrillation or other arrhythmias

occasional.symptomName: Peripheral edema due to right heart failure
occasional.notes: Dependent edema from impaired venous return
searchTerms: swelling in legs from heart problems
ankle puffiness due to heart failure
unintentional weight loss and poor appetite

occasional.symptomName: Hoarseness due to recurrent laryngeal nerve involvement
searchTerms: hoarse voice due to nerve involvement

rare.notes: Transient loss of consciousness from impaired cardiac output
searchTerms: fainting due to heart fluid pressure
passing out caused by heart compression

laboratory: Possible mild anemia of chronic disease
imaging: Echocardiography showing pericardial effusion and thickening
CT/MRI demonstrating irregular pericardial mass or nodular thickening
PET scan showing increased metabolic activity in pericardium
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; asbestos exposure history relevant

distinguishingFeatures: Immunohistochemical markers negative for mesothelial origin
History of infection or autoimmune disease
Absence of malignant cells on biopsy

redFlags: Rapidly progressive pericardial effusion with tamponade
Unexplained constrictive pericarditis refractory to treatment
Presence of pericardial mass on imaging
references: Robinson BW, Lake RA. Advances in malignant mesothelioma. N Engl J Med. 2005;353(15):1591-603.
Maisch B, Seferović PM, Ristić AD, et al. Guidelines on the diagnosis and management of pericardial diseases. Eur Heart J. 2004;25(7):587-610.
